Chief"Moriuji has left Fudaraku. He will be here shortly."
Kageaki"Understood."
Chief"Are you ready?"
Kageaki"To take a real priest's place, everything is arranged. Two minutes also it will not take."
Chief"Good. ...You still intend to strike at the Lower Shrine?"
Kageaki"Yes."
Chief"The Grand Commander's men may already be hiding there. Not even a remote chance of that? This one thing is troubling me."
Kageaki"I have checked it repeatedly. Muramasa is making the final check now—"

————How was this happening? Kya ho raha hai?


Armor she had been. Armor.


Then a spider. Eight legs, still some connection to the armor business.


From there, straight to a young woman one fine day? What bloody logic was doing this?

She was not some grateful crane from a folktale, coming to repay a favor. Even the folktales had their own procedures.

What to do, I did not know. Several times I had seen this form already. Each time, the understanding refused to come with it.

Not understanding at all. Magnificently not understanding.

Ask me what precisely was troubling me, and even that I could not explain. My brain had been given this situation to digest and was refusing the food.

At least if Muramasa had remained steel, something I could have managed. A steel woman, fine. Some connection with the previous condition. But...

en.html:
For the Prince and the Chief, my deciding not to kill Moriuji was not the worst possibility. Decide to kill him, attack, then start wavering halfway and let him escape—that was the disaster.

Full disaster, properly completed. The assassination had to succeed and throw the shogunate into confusion. Only then could the Prince find a way to survive, even if people suspected him of arranging it.

“Assassination we attempted. Moriuji is perfectly fine.” Give that report, and His Highness's soul would certainly be leaving for the unseen world.

...If things approached that point, the Chief probably meant to warn the Prince and get him away.

Little chance of success, but much better than nothing.

Not that I could take comfort in this arrangement. Their last chance was not my cushion.

ja.html:
親王と署長にとって最も望ましくない事態とは、俺
が護氏を殺さないと決断することではない。
　一旦は殺すと決めて襲いながら、途中で迷い、挙句
取り逃がしてしまうことだ。

　これはまさしく最悪である。
　大将領暗殺に成功して幕府が大きな動揺をきたせば
こそ、たとえ黒幕だと感付かれても親王は生存の道を
得られるのだ。

　暗殺は試みたが護氏は無事でした、では間違いなく
親王の霊魂が<ruby>幽世<rt>かくりよ</rt></ruby>へ旅立つ。
　……その最悪の事態が迫った時、署長は親王に急を
知らせて逃亡させるつもりなのだろう。

　成功の見込みは薄いが、やらぬよりは余程いい。

　無論、俺はその手配りで安心してはならないわけだ
が。
